title: The $7.2M FTC Fine Against HomeAdvisor, Explained for Contractors
h1: The $7.2 Million FTC Fine Against HomeAdvisor — What It Means for You
meta: The FTC ordered HomeAdvisor to pay up to $7.2M for misleading contractors about lead quality (FTC 2023). Here's what the case says about buying leads.
short: In 2023 the FTC ordered HomeAdvisor to pay up to $7.2 million for selling contractors leads it described as high-quality and exclusive that often weren't. It's a regulator putting the shared-lead model on the record.
statLabel: FTC order against HomeAdvisor for misleading contractors on lead quality (FTC 2023)

body.answer: A federal regulator put the shared-lead model on the record.
body.html: In 2023 the Federal Trade Commission ordered HomeAdvisor to pay up to $7.2 million (FTC 2023) to settle charges it misled contractors about the quality and source of the leads it sold — including leads pitched as high-quality and exclusive that frequently were neither.

body.answer: Leads oversold on quality; an upsell many didn't grasp.
body.html: The complaint centered on how leads were marketed: contractors were told they'd get high-quality, in-market leads, and many didn't. There were also concerns about how the optional membership and lead volume were presented at sign-up. You don't have to be a lawyer to read the signal.

body.h2: What it means for your money
body.answer: You can't audit a lead you don't control.
body.html: The takeaway isn't that one company is uniquely bad. It's that when you rent leads, you can't see how they were generated, who else got them, or whether they were ever real intent. Leads you generate — your Google profile, your site, your referrals — are the ones you can actually trust and measure.

body.answer: This one came straight off the podcast.
body.html: Marshall and Ray went deep on this in Is Angi Worth It? on Get Booked, Not F***ed — same math, more cussing. Watch or listen to the full episode here.

faq.q: Did HomeAdvisor have to pay $7.2 million?
faq.a: The FTC's 2023 order required HomeAdvisor to pay up to $7.2 million to settle charges it misled contractors about lead quality and source (FTC 2023).

faq.q: Is Angi the same company as HomeAdvisor?
faq.a: They operate under the same corporate umbrella. The FTC case was specifically about HomeAdvisor's lead marketing to contractors.

faq.q: Does this mean I should never buy leads?
faq.a: Not necessarily — but it's a strong reason to treat rented leads as a risk you can't audit, and to invest first in leads you own and can measure.
